methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective single-institution cohort of 154 adult Ph+ B-ALL patients spanning 2001-2019, appropriate to a descriptive outcomes question but inherently vulnerable to selection bias and secular confounding from improvements in supportive care and TKI evolution. The authors sensibly stratified by induction time period (2001-2009, 2010-2015, 2016-2019) and modeled alloSCT as a time-varying covariate in Cox regression to mitigate immortal-time bias, which is a methodological strength. However, no a priori power calculation is reported, subgroup sizes are small (only 23 non-transplant patients in 2016-2019 drive the headline 87% OS), no multiplicity correction is applied across the many univariate tests in Table 2, and handling of missing data (unknown donor, unknown TKI) and sensitivity analyses are not described. The absence of cytogenetic/molecular (IKZF1) data, acknowledged in the Discussion, materially constrains causal interpretation of the alloSCT hazard ratios.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort of consecutive adult Ph+ B-ALL patients at a single institution, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question of whether routine CR1 alloSCT can be safely omitted in patients achieving adequate BCR::ABL1 MRD response on a pediatric-inspired chemotherapy plus imatinib backbone is highly relevant and directly aligned with evolving NCCN guidance versus EBMT/ASTCT recommendations. Endpoints are patient-centered (OS, RFS) with long follow-up (median 41 months, range up to 228 months), and the reported 4-year OS of 87% in the contemporary non-transplant cohort provides translationally meaningful real-world evidence supporting MRD-guided omission of alloSCT. The findings reinforce rather than overturn an already-shifting paradigm, which prevents a top score.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies as this is an observational cohort study. Key STROBE items are addressed: setting, participants (with explicit exclusions of 3 patients), outcome and relapse definitions, statistical methods, confounder handling via time-period stratification, and limitations discussed. However, no STROBE checklist is cited, no participant flow diagram is provided, missing-data handling is unaddressed, and some per-subgroup denominators are stated inconsistently (e.g., 141 of 154 vs. 141 of 157 CR1 patients). There is no data availability statement, no mention of code or scripts (SAS 9.4 is named but no analysis code is referenced), and no indication that de-identified data could be shared, so reproducibility posture is minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical novelty is incremental: multiple prior groups cited in the paper itself (Ravandi 2013, Short 2016, Jabbour 2018, Badar 2023) have already reported favorable outcomes in Ph+ B-ALL patients treated with chemotherapy plus TKI without routine CR1 alloSCT. The distinctive contributions are the long single-center follow-up (up to ~19 years), the specific pediatric-inspired PM-DFCI backbone with imatinib (versus HyperCVAD in most comparators), and documentation of iterative asparaginase omission as a separate protocol change. The positioning in the introduction and discussion is thorough and comparators are appropriately acknowledged without over-claiming firsts, placing this as a meaningful extension rather than a paradigm-shifting result.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear narrative arc: evolving protocol modifications motivated in the introduction, methods matched to those changes, results stratified accordingly, and a comprehensive discussion that contextualizes each finding against the literature. Acronyms are generally expanded on first use (TKI, alloSCT, MRD, CMR), and the abstract is quantitatively grounded with concrete OS/RFS endpoints. Minor issues include a typographic anomaly (95% CI 64.8.1-95.6) and some repetition between results and discussion regarding the 87% OS figure; figure/table captions are inferred to be adequate but not evaluable here. Overall clarity and precision are appropriate for a specialist hematology audience.

key_strengths: Long, consecutive single-center cohort (2001-2019) with median 41-month follow-up supporting a clinically meaningful MRD-guided deintensification message
Appropriate use of time-varying alloSCT covariate in Cox regression, mitigating immortal-time bias
Time-period stratification (2001-2009, 2010-2015, 2016-2019) directly aligns analysis with the two protocol changes under evaluation
Thorough and balanced positioning against UKALLXII, UKALL14, Ravandi, Short, Jabbour, D-ALBA, and GIMEMA ALL2820 literature
Direct alignment with current NCCN guidance, enhancing translational relevance
key_concerns: Headline 87% 4-year OS rests on only 23 patients in the 2016-2019 non-transplant subgroup; wide CIs and limited power
No a priori sample-size calculation, no multiplicity correction across many univariate tests, no formal missing-data handling or sensitivity analysis
Residual confounding from unmeasured cytogenetic/molecular features (IKZF1, IKZFplus) acknowledged but not addressed analytically
No data availability statement and no reference to analytic code; reproducibility posture is weak
Minor internal numeric inconsistencies (141/154 vs 141/157 for CR1) and a typo in a confidence interval (64.8.1-95.6)
Novelty is incremental: multiple prior series have already supported MRD-guided omission of CR1 alloSCT
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently conducted, well-written retrospective single-center cohort that adds confirmatory real-world evidence to an already-shifting paradigm; methodological limitations and small contemporary subgroup size preclude a higher tier, but the findings are clinically relevant and appropriate for a mid-tier oncology journal (approximate JIF 4-9.9) with minor revisions.
